4533.text: In Prov.17.19 'seeks destruction' is a figurative/idiomatic extension of baqash's base gloss (seek to find/secure); rather than literal pursuit of an object, it describes the unintended but inevitable consequence courted by prideful behaviour -- a nuance of self-incurred ruin distinct from the term's more common sense of deliberately pursuing a desired good (e.g. Gen.25.22's seeking of the Lord, Ps.10.15's judicial demand).

4534.text: No prior context recorded. Other M-codes in Prov.17.19 -- M51 'loves' (twice), M56 'transgression', M10 'strife', M08 'high/pride' -- form a chain of causes (love of transgression/strife, pride) that baqash's 'seeks destruction' names as their outcome; the seeking-characteristic thus functions as the terminal consequence-marker for the preceding dispositional M-codes rather than being directly related to any single one of them.

6646.text: In Ezek.34.6 'seek' (paired with H1875 'search') describes shepherds' neglect of the sheep, sitting within the base sense of active caretaking-seeking without further divergence.

6661.text: In Ezek.34.6 'search' activates the pastoral-care/diligent-tending sense of darash (caring for lost sheep) rather than the cultic consult-God sense, a shepherding-specific nuance with the impact of framing the shepherds' negligence as a failure of basic pastoral duty, not merely a failure of religious devotion; this differs markedly from its use of seeking God in Jer.29.13.

6677.text: In Ezek.34.6 the seeking (paired with H1875) is negated -- 'none to search or seek' -- meaning the shepherds who should be the initiating party toward the scattered sheep (the target) are absent from performing the operation, itself the verse's core indictment.

6679.text: In Ezek.34.6 'search' (darash) is negated together with H1245 -- 'none to search or seek for them' -- the shepherds who should initiate the caring-search toward the scattered sheep are absent, the operation's non-performance is the point.

6689.text: M76 (wandering/straying) and M22 (height, 'high hill') co-occur alongside H1875 (also home cluster): the negated seeking (paired with H1875) is presented as the direct remedy that ought to have addressed the sheep's wandering (M76) but did not -- seeking's absence is causally tied to the wandering's continuation.

6691.text: Building on H1245's note for this verse: darash's own vantage adds the specifically pastoral-care dimension to the negated search -- it is not just general seeking (H1245) but the diligent shepherding-inquiry (H1875) that is absent, doubling the indictment of the shepherds' neglect toward the wandering (M76) sheep.

7081.text: Ezek.34.6 and Ezek.34.11 both use 'search' of shepherding care for scattered sheep -- one negated (no shepherd searches) and one emphatic (God himself will search) -- forming a matched pair where the pastoral-care sense of darash is activated on both the human failure side and the divine remedy side of the same extended shepherd metaphor.

19651.text: Isaiah 7:15–16 — "when he knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good": The setting is a king’s heart in fear. Syria and Ephraim are marching on Jerusalem, and *"the heart of Ahaz and the heart of his people shook as the trees of the forest shake before the wind"* (v2). The Lord sends Isaiah with a word for that heart: *"Be careful, be quiet, do not fear, and do not let your heart be faint"* (v4); the threat *"shall not stand"* (v7); then the condition: *"If you are not firm in faith, you will not be firm at all"* (v9). Both "firm" words are the one verb (H0539), so standing firm and being kept firm are the same word.; Then the Lord makes Ahaz an offer: *"Ask a sign of the Lord your God; let it be deep as Sheol or high as heaven"* (v11). Ahaz refuses, in pious words: *"I will not ask, and I will not put the Lord to the test"* (v12). The answer shows what that refusal was: *"Is it too little for you to weary men, that you weary my God also?"* (v13). Ahaz’s refusal was a choice. He chose not to take hold of what the Lord held out.; The sign is given anyway, and at its centre is a child who has what Ahaz lacked: *"He shall eat curds and honey when he knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good"* (v15). The act is one act with two sides: refusing the evil (H3988A); choosing the good (H0977); Refusing is not a step before the choice. It is the choice seen from the other side. Both rest on a knowing: *"when he knows how"*. The verse marks the moment a person can tell evil from good and turn from the one to the other.; The verse ties the eating to that knowing: he eats *"when he knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good"*. The oracle itself says what curds and honey are. *"In that day … because of the abundance of milk that they give, he will eat curds, for everyone who is left in the land will eat curds and honey"* (v21–22). It is the food of those left in the land after the Lord has swept it with *"the king of Assyria"*: vineyards turned to *"briers and thorns"*, hills *"where cattle are let loose"* (v23–25). The child who refuses the evil and chooses the good eats with those who are left, and eats from abundance, in a land stripped of what it had.

20258.text: Deuteronomy 18:6: "and he may come when he desires": Two choosings stand in the passage. First the tribe: *"For the Lord your God has chosen him out of all your tribes to stand and minister in the name of the Lord, him and his sons for all time"* (v5). Then the place: a Levite living in any town *"may come when he desires—to the place that the Lord will choose, and ministers in the name of the Lord his God, like all his fellow Levites"* (v6–7).; "When he desires" is literally "with all the desire of his soul": *kol* (all; H3605) with *ʾawwāh* (desire; H0185) and *nepeš* (*soul: appetite*; H5315L). It is the same desire of the soul that is given room for meat in Deu 12:20–21. Here it is turned toward the chosen place.; The Levite has no land: *"They shall have no inheritance among their brothers; the Lord is their inheritance, as he promised them"* (v2). The law secures his share when he comes: *"then he may have equal portions to eat"* (v8).
